title: bug: mysql migration error
body:
### Describe the bug

Haven't used Homarr for a while (my entire swarm blew up; long story) and just tried firing up Homarr using the `:latest` tag and I get this in the log before it crashes:

```
  cause: Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near '(select coalesce(json_arrayagg(json_array(`boards_sections`.`id`, `boards_sec...' at line 1
      at /app/db/migrations/mysql/migrate.cjs:72995:27
      at MySql2PreparedQuery.queryWithCache (/app/db/migrations/mysql/migrate.cjs:72816:22)
      at MySql2PreparedQuery.execute (/app/db/migrations/mysql/migrate.cjs:72994:31)
      at QueryPromise.execute (/app/db/migrations/mysql/migrate.cjs:72542:27)
      at QueryPromise.then (/app/db/migrations/mysql/migrate.cjs:66816:17)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5) {
    code: 'ER_PARSE_ERROR',
    errno: 1064,
    sqlState: '42000',
    sqlMessage: "You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MariaDB server version for the right syntax to use near '(select coalesce(json_arrayagg(json_array(`boards_sections`.`id`, `boards_sec...' at line 1",
    sql: 'select `boards`.`id`, `boards`.`name`, `boards`.`is_public`, `boards`.`creator_id`, `boards`.`page_title`, `boards`.`meta_title`, `boards`.`logo_image_url`, `boards`.`favicon_image_url`, `boards`.`background_image_url`, `boards`.`background_image_attachment`, `boards`.`background_image_repeat`, `boards`.`background_image_size`, `boards`.`primary_color`, `boards`.`secondary_color`, `boards`.`opacity`, `boards`.`custom_css`, `boards`.`icon_color`, `boards`.`item_radius`, `boards`.`disable_status`, `boards_sections`.`data` as `sections`, `boards_layouts`.`data` as `layouts` from `board` `boards` left join lateral (select coalesce(json_arrayagg(json_array(`boards_sections`.`id`, `boards_sections`.`board_id`, `boards_sections`.`kind`, `boards_sections`.`x_offset`, `boards_sections`.`y_offset`, `boards_sections`.`name`, `boards_sections`.`options`)), json_array()) as `data` from `section` `boards_sections` where `boards_sections`.`board_id` = `boards`.`id`) `boards_sections` on true left join lateral (select coalesce(json_arrayagg(json_array(`boards_layouts`.`id`, `boards_layouts`.`name`, `boards_layouts`.`board_id`, `boards_layouts`.`column_count`, `boards_layouts`.`breakpoint`)), json_array()) as `data` from `layout` `boards_layouts` where `boards_layouts`.`board_id` = `boards`.`id`) `boards_layouts` on true limit 1'
  }
}
ERROR: DB migrations failed, aborting startup
```

Is there any quick-n-easy-fix?

### Steps to reproduce

I guess:

1. Be using an older version of Homarr
2. Have your Docker Swarm take a huge, steaming shite
3. Rip your hair out getting that working again
4. Fire up the latest Homarr
5. Rip your hair out some more because it crashes on startup
6. Come here

### Impact

Use Organizerr instead? `*shrug*`

### Additional information

_No response_

### Version

1.73.0

### Installation method

Portainer

### Browser

Brave

full_comments.body:
Thanks for the report, I'll look into it and try fixing the migration files. It's strange that this wasn't caught because we have a test to apply these migrations. 


Honestly I would recommend just using the built in SQLite version in the meantime, less configuration and much better performance. We might remove support for MySQL entirely in the future as there are less than 10 users of it

> Thanks for the report, I'll look into it and try fixing the migration files. It's strange that this wasn't caught because we have a test to apply these migrations.

That pretty much sums up my entire existence; I'm always the one and only to have even the most obscure bug rear its head as soon as I go to use it (any app or product).

> Honestly I would recommend just using the built in SQLite version in the meantime, less configuration and much better performance. We might remove support for MySQL entirely in the future as there are less than 10 users of it

I personally tend to prefer either mysql or postgres over sqlite, especially in a swarm, because I can keep all of my apps' DBs in one nice, tidy UI (ie phpadmin) and don't have to mess around with using other apps to keep the db in sync across nodes (ie setting up something like syncthing to watch for changes).
Your use case makes sense, we'll keep postgresql for now. I think syncthing for sqlite would be a nightmare to deal with 😆
